title: 1998 AHSME Problem 3
statement: If \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are digits for which \[ \begin{array}{r} 7a2\\ {}-48b\\ \hline c73 \end{array} \] then \(a+b+c=\)

solutions.text: The units column gives \(12-b=3,\) so \(b=9.\) In the tens column, \(a-1\) must borrow, and \(a-1+10-8=7,\) giving \(a=6.\) The hundreds column then gives \(7-1-4=c=2.\) Therefore \(a+b+c=6+9+2=17,\) so D is correct.
